# Test vectors: throwaway Canton 3.6.1 keys

**Every key in `vectors/` is a disposable test key.** They were generated by a throwaway Canton
3.6.1 participant with in-memory storage, bound to 127.0.0.1, that never connected to a
synchronizer and was shut down right after the export. None of these keys ever belonged to any
network, node or party. Do not reuse them for anything.

The password used for the password-protected exports is public on purpose:
`rutli-test-vector-password` (also in `vectors/manifest.json`).

## What is here

For each key `<name>` (see `vectors/manifest.json` for fingerprint, purpose, key spec, usage):

| File | What it is | Canton source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>.export.bin` | `keys.secret.download(fp)` = `ExportKeyPair` without password: `UntypedVersionedMessage(30)` around `CryptoKeyPair` | `GrpcVaultService.scala:584-706` |
| `<name>.export-pw.bin` | the same with a password: `UntypedVersionedMessage(30)` around `PasswordBasedEncrypted` | `GrpcVaultService.scala:684-698`, `PasswordBasedEncryption.scala` |
| `<name>.stored.bin` | the bytes `common_crypto_private_keys.data` holds for an unwrapped key: `privateKey.toByteString(pv)` | `CryptoPrivateStoreExtended.scala:226, 303` |
| `<name>.pub.bin` | `keys.public.download(fp)`: `UntypedVersionedMessage(30)` around `SigningPublicKey` / `EncryptionPublicKey` | `VaultAdministration.scala:779-797` |

Keys: the three a participant creates at auto-init (`namespace` Ed25519, `signing` Ed25519 protocol,
`sequencer-auth` Ed25519, `encryption` ECIES P-256) plus `extra-ecp256-signing` (EC P-256,
protocol) and `extra-rsa2048-encryption` (RSA-2048), generated by the script. Canton 3.6.1 gives
the participant separate `signing` and `sequencer-auth` keys.

`stored.bin` is produced by the generator script calling Canton's own serializer on the exported
key (the in-memory store has no database to dump); it is byte-identical to what the DB store writes.

## Regenerating

```sh
CANTON_HOME=~/.cache/canton-3.6.1/canton-open-source-3.6.1 \
JAVA_HOME=/path/to/an/openjdk \
  frost/canton-key/testdata/gen/generate.sh
```

Use an **OpenJDK** build (17+; Homebrew's `openjdk` 26 works). Oracle's JDK refuses the
password-protected export with `JCE cannot authenticate the provider BC`, because Canton's fat jar
bundles an unsigned BouncyCastle and Oracle's JCE only loads signed providers for `Cipher`.

Keys are random, so regenerating replaces every file; commit the whole `vectors/` directory and
re-run `cargo test -p rutli-canton-key`.
